name: The Cliffs of Moher & the Burren
tagline: Ireland's most famous sea cliffs and a strange, beautiful limestone landscape found almost nowhere else in Europe.
highlight: Walking the cliff-edge path near O'Brien's Tower as the Atlantic crashes 200 metres below and the full curve of the cliffs comes into view.
shortDescription: Sheer 200-metre Atlantic cliffs and the otherworldly limestone karst of the Burren, two of Ireland's most striking natural landscapes side by side in County Clare.
metaDescription: A Cliffs of Moher and Burren travel guide: the cliff walks, Poulnabrone Dolmen, the Burren's limestone landscape, food and how to plan a visit to County Clare.
knownFor: The Cliffs of Moher, the Burren's limestone landscape, Doolin's music pubs

image.alt: The Cliffs of Moher rising sheer from the Atlantic Ocean

intro: The Cliffs of Moher are genuinely Ireland's most photographed natural landmark, rising up to 214 metres straight out of the Atlantic along an eight-kilometre stretch of County Clare's coastline.

Just inland lies the Burren, a genuinely strange and beautiful limestone karst landscape unlike anywhere else in Ireland, its bare grey pavement hiding rare Arctic and Mediterranean wildflowers in its cracks alongside one of Europe's densest concentrations of ancient tombs.
Most visitors genuinely combine the two as a single day trip or overnight from Galway or the Dingle Peninsula, basing themselves in the small music-pub village of Doolin at the region's edge.

whyVisit.intro: The Cliffs of Moher and the Burren's case rests on genuinely dramatic, easily accessible natural scenery unlike anywhere else on the island.

points.title: The cliffs are genuinely as dramatic as the photos suggest
points.text: A sheer 214-metre drop to the Atlantic, with a well-built cliff-edge path running the full length.

points.title: The Burren is genuinely unlike anywhere else in Ireland
points.text: A bare limestone karst landscape hiding rare wildflowers and one of Europe's densest concentrations of ancient tombs.

points.title: Poulnabrone Dolmen is genuinely older than Stonehenge
points.text: A Neolithic portal tomb dating back roughly 5,800 years, standing alone in the open karst.

points.title: Doolin's pub sessions are genuinely among Ireland's best
points.text: A tiny village with an outsized reputation for authentic, nightly traditional music.

points.title: It works genuinely well as a day trip or a slower overnight
points.text: Reachable from Galway or the Dingle Peninsula in either direction.

attractionsIntro: The essential sights split between the Atlantic drama of the cliffs and the quiet strangeness of the Burren just inland.

attractions.name: The Cliffs of Moher

image.alt: The sheer Atlantic cliffs of the Cliffs of Moher

attractions.text: Genuinely Ireland's best-known natural landmark, rising up to 214 metres above the Atlantic along an eight-kilometre stretch of coastline.
attractions.tip: Visit genuinely early morning or late afternoon for softer light and noticeably thinner crowds.

attractions.name: O'Brien's Tower

image.file: File:O'Brien's Tower, Cliffs Of Moher - geograph.org.uk - 5738168.jpg
image.alt: O'Brien's Tower at the highest point of the Cliffs of Moher

attractions.text: A genuinely photogenic 19th-century viewing tower at the cliffs' highest point, built in 1835 for Victorian-era tourists.
attractions.tip: Climb genuinely to the top for the single best panoramic view of the full cliff line.

attractions.name: The Burren

image.alt: The limestone karst landscape of the Burren in County Clare

attractions.text: A genuinely strange, beautiful limestone karst landscape found almost nowhere else in Europe, its cracks sheltering rare Arctic and Mediterranean plants side by side.
attractions.tip: Genuinely look closely at the limestone cracks (grikes) — the rare wildflowers hide in their sheltered microclimate.

attractions.name: Poulnabrone Dolmen

image.alt: Poulnabrone Dolmen, a Neolithic portal tomb in the Burren

attractions.text: A genuinely striking Neolithic portal tomb standing alone in the open karst, dating back roughly 5,800 years, older than Stonehenge.
attractions.tip: Genuinely free to visit, with a small roadside car park and a short walk across the limestone.

attractions.name: Doolin village

image.file: File:Doolin - Fisher Street - Village Area - Colourful Buildings at East End of Street - geograph.org.uk - 3131002.jpg
image.alt: The colourful village of Doolin in County Clare

attractions.text: A genuinely tiny village with an outsized reputation as one of Ireland's best spots for authentic traditional music sessions.
attractions.tip: Genuinely book accommodation well ahead in summer — Doolin's small size means it fills fast.

attractions.name: Aillwee Cave

image.alt: The underground passages of Aillwee Cave in the Burren

attractions.text: A genuinely accessible show cave running deep into the Burren's limestone, with guided tours past underground waterfalls and ancient bear pits.
attractions.tip: Genuinely bring a light jacket — the cave stays a constant, cool temperature year-round.

attractions.name: Kilfenora & the Burren Centre

image.alt: The Burren Centre in Kilfenora, County Clare

attractions.text: A genuinely small village anchoring the Burren, home to a cathedral with High Crosses and an interpretive centre explaining the region's unique geology.
attractions.tip: Genuinely worth a stop to understand the Burren's landscape before exploring it further.

thingsToDoIntro: The region genuinely rewards a mix of cliff-edge walking and slower time in the Burren's quieter landscape.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the Cliffs of Moher coastal path

image.alt: Walkers on the coastal path at the Cliffs of Moher

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely well-maintained path runs the length of the cliffs, with the quieter southern stretch toward Hag's Head often less crowded.
thingsToDo.tip: Stay genuinely behind the safety fencing — the cliff edges are a real, serious hazard in wind.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Poulnabrone Dolmen up close

image.alt: Poulnabrone Dolmen standing in the open Burren landscape

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely short, easy walk across open limestone to one of Ireland's most photographed ancient monuments.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely visit early or late in the day to have the site largely to yourself.

thingsToDo.title: Go underground at Aillwee Cave

image.alt: A guided tour inside Aillwee Cave

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely accessible guided tour into the Burren's underground world, good for a rainy-day alternative to the cliffs.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely combine with the on-site farm shop's cheese, made from the surrounding Burren pasture.

thingsToDo.title: Spot rare Burren wildflowers

image.file: File:Native Flowers and the Karst Landscape at the Burren, Clare.jpg
image.alt: Wildflowers growing in the limestone cracks of the Burren

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely unusual botanical mix of Arctic, alpine and Mediterranean species growing side by side, found almost nowhere else on Earth.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely late spring brings the widest variety of Burren wildflowers into bloom.

thingsToDo.title: Hear trad music in a Doolin pub

image.file: File:Doolin - Fisher Street - Village Area - Aille River, White Horse, R459 - geograph.org.uk - 3131033.jpg
image.alt: A traditional music pub in Doolin village

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential Doolin evening, with several small pubs hosting some of Ireland's most respected nightly sessions.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely arrive early for a seat near the musicians — Doolin's sessions draw a loyal crowd.

thingsToDo.title: Drive the Burren's open karst plateau

image.file: File:Limestone landscape in The Burren, Co Clare, Ireland - geograph.org.uk - 7687735.jpg
image.alt: A road crossing the open limestone plateau of the Burren

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely otherworldly drive across bare grey limestone terraces, unlike any other landscape in Ireland.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely stop often — the Burren's scale and strangeness are best appreciated slowly, not from a moving car.

bestTime.headline: May, June and September for the clearest views and thinner crowds
bestTime.summary: The cliffs are genuinely visitable year-round, though clear days for the best views are far more likely outside midsummer.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Cliffs of Moher and Burren visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Visit genuinely early morning or late afternoon to avoid the busiest midday tour bus crowds.
Check the genuinely weather forecast before going — low cloud can hide the cliffs completely.
Stay genuinely behind the safety fencing at all times — the cliff edges are a real, serious hazard.
Book Doolin accommodation genuinely well ahead in summer given the village's small size.
Wear genuinely sturdy shoes and a windproof layer, even on an apparently calm day.
Combine genuinely the cliffs with the Burren rather than choosing one — they're a short drive apart.

faq.q: How many days do you need for the Cliffs of Moher and the Burren?
faq.a: One to two days genuinely covers both comfortably, and the cliffs alone are an easy half-day visit.

faq.q: Can you visit the Cliffs of Moher as a day trip from Galway?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — it's about a ninety-minute drive each way, and organised day tours run regularly.

faq.q: Is the Cliffs of Moher walk difficult?
faq.a: No, genuinely accessible — the main path is well maintained and mostly flat, though the full length is a few hours round trip.

faq.q: What is the Burren known for?
faq.a: Genuinely its unusual limestone karst landscape, hiding rare Arctic and Mediterranean wildflowers alongside one of Europe's densest concentrations of ancient tombs.
Yes, genuinely — it's small, but its traditional music pubs are among Ireland's most respected, and it sits close to both the cliffs and the Burren.
Genuinely around 5,800 years old, a Neolithic portal tomb older than Stonehenge and England's other famous prehistoric monuments.
